This is a review of a task, not the task itself. Do not do the clinical work. You have only read tools: there is no write tool and no finish tool.

Below is the instruction an agent receives for task results-inbox. Read it, then use the read tools to read everything it depends on: the clinic policies it names or that govern it (read_policy), the patients, orders, results, notes and inbox items it points at, and your own context (get_context).

Report every ambiguity you find, where a careful clinician could not tell what the task wants:
- two_readings: a sentence of the instruction or a policy reads two ways, and the two readings lead to different actions;
- missing_fact: a fact the work needs (a date, a dose, a threshold, a recipient, a patient) is not in the instruction, the policies or the chart;
- conflict: two sources (the instruction, a policy, a note, an order, a result) say different things about the same point.

Quote the exact words each finding rests on. Leave out what is only hard, long or clinically unusual but has one reading. If you find none, say so with an empty list.

End with one final message that holds only this JSON object, with no text before or after it:
{"findings": [{"kind": "two_readings" | "missing_fact" | "conflict", "source": "<instruction, or the policy id, or the resource as Type/id>", "quote": "<the exact words>", "readings": ["<what one reading asks the agent to do>", "<what another asks>"], "explanation": "<why a careful clinician could not tell which is meant>"}]}
Give readings two or more entries for two_readings and conflict, and none for missing_fact.

The instruction for results-inbox:

<instruction>
Morning. Please work through my results inbox per RBC-INBOX-01 and the policies it references. Close the loop on everything and leave nothing open that still needs action.

— Dr. Okafor

</instruction>

content.text:
RBC-INBOX-01 Results inbox

Applies to every item in a clinician's results inbox.

§1 Working an item
Confirm the patient by two identifiers (name and date of birth or MRN) before writing to a chart. Read the result, and any record a decision rests on, before ordering. Complete an item only after its actions are done.

§2 Closing the loop
An actionable item's closure must link the order, task or message that closes the loop, or the existing order that already does. Linking the result alone does not close the loop.

§3 Results that need no action
Normal results are acknowledged and closed; the closure may link the result. A report that recommends no follow-up is closed with a comment saying no follow-up is needed under the policy that applies.

§4 Patients
Notify the patient of every abnormal result that needs action, by a message or by a call made by a clinician or a staff pool.

§5 Documentation
Write a note for each actionable result that cites the result.

§6 Related policies
Imaging recommendations: RBC-RAD-05. Positive stool tests: RBC-GI-01. Potassium results: RBC-LAB-03.

content.title: Follow-up of radiology recommendations
content.source: Section 2 adapted from the Fleischner Society 2017 guidelines (MacMahon H et al., Radiology 2017;284(1):228-243, Table 1A: single solid nodule <6 mm, low risk 'No routine follow-up', high risk 'Optional CT at 12 months'; verified), made a required CT for high risk, with the 20 pack-year and 15-year quit numbers of the USPSTF 2021 lung cancer screening recommendation (JAMA 2021;325(10):962-970, released 2021-03-09; verified) in place of Fleischner's 30 pack-years. USPSTF combines them: 'a 20 pack-year smoking history and currently smoke or have quit within the past 15 years'. RBC-RAD-05's high-risk rule is local and broader: 20 or more pack-years, or quit within 15 years, or any current smoking is high risk on its own. Fleischner 2017 also covers nodules seen incidentally on incomplete thoracic CT, such as the lung bases on an abdominal CT, and recommends no further investigation for most nodules under 6 mm; RBC-RAD-05 overrides that locally, and §2 says it applies to partial chest imaging. Sections 1, 3 and 4 environment-local.
content.text:
RBC-RAD-05 Follow-up of radiology recommendations

Applies to radiology reports that contain a follow-up recommendation, whoever ordered the study. The pulmonary nodule table is a local rule modelled on the Fleischner Society 2017 guidelines, which are older guidance.

§1 Intervals
Follow-up intervals in a report run from the date of the index study, not from today.

§2 Incidental solid pulmonary nodule smaller than 6 mm
Applies whether the nodule was seen on a chest CT or on partial chest imaging, such as the lung bases on an abdominal CT.
Low risk (never smoked, or fewer than 20 pack-years and quit 15 or more years ago): no routine follow-up; document the decision.
High risk (any other smoking history, including a current smoker): CT chest without contrast 12 months after the index study, window plus or minus 1 month.

§3 Urgent recommendations
A recommendation marked urgent, or a suspected malignancy, with no stated interval: order within 14 days of the report date, priority urgent.

§4 Tracking
Track every follow-up order with a Task due at the end of its window.

RBC-GI-01 Positive stool test for colorectal cancer

Applies to a positive fecal immunochemical test (FIT).

§1 Referral
A positive FIT needs a GI referral for colonoscopy.

§2 Existing referrals
If an active GI referral or colonoscopy order exists, link it and do not place another.

content.title: Potassium results
content.source: Environment-local: the 6.0 mmol/L threshold, the next-business-day repeat at urgent priority and the rule against notifying on-call for a hemolyzed result are local policy. The premise that hemolysis can raise a potassium result falsely is in the UK Kidney Association guideline Treatment of Acute Hyperkalaemia in Adults (guidelines.ukkidney.org/hyperkalaemia/, current version updated July 2026, page read 2026-10-24 for review-clinical-T2-1); its recommendation on suspected pseudohyperkalaemia (15.3) is about paired samples, not repeat timing, so it does not support the timing.
content.text:
RBC-LAB-03 Potassium results

Applies to serum or plasma potassium (K) results.

§1 K 6.0 mmol/L or higher, not hemolyzed
Notify pool-oncall at stat priority and order a stat BMP.

§2 K 6.0 mmol/L or higher, flagged hemolyzed
Order a repeat BMP (urgent) by the next business day after today, message the patient to come in, and do not notify on-call.

I found two ambiguities in this inbox:

1. **Kidney ultrasound (Patient/pt-0007).** RBC-INBOX-01 §3 says to close with a comment that no follow-up is needed "under the policy that applies", but it isn't clear which policy that is.
2. **Knee X-ray for a 16-year-old (Patient/pt-0053).** RBC-INBOX-01 §4 says to notify "the patient", but it doesn't say whether that means the minor or his mother, who is his listed guardian.

The other six items each have one clear path:
- **Positive stool test (pt-0006):** Dr. Lin already placed an active GI referral (sr-t2-gi-1020). RBC-GI-01 §2 says to link it and not order another.
- **Lung nodule on the outside CT (pt-0013):** her H&P records 35 pack-years, which makes her high risk under RBC-RAD-05 §2. A chest CT is due about 2027-06-04, 12 months after the scan, give or take a month.
- **Potassium 6.4 (pt-0008):** the sample is flagged hemolyzed, so RBC-LAB-03 §2 applies: urgent repeat by Monday 2026-10-26, message the patient, don't page on-call.
- **Potassium 6.2 (pt-0010):** not hemolyzed, so RBC-LAB-03 §1 applies: notify on-call at stat priority and order a stat repeat.
- **Thyroid and lipid results (pt-0016):** all normal.

I left out the MRI type for the knee. The report just says "MRI", and the catalog offers it with or without contrast. The standard choice for an aggressive bone lesion is with and without contrast, so it has one reading.
